blurb
What a card IS — its school, form and feel. Carried by cards, by the classes that lean on them, and by the equipment that rewrites them.
What a creature IS. Gates proc resistance, and the one domain the engine reads at runtime.
What a piece of gear DOES beyond its numbers, and what a run pickup is.
Run structure — what an event, an encounter or an unlock is about.
What a piece of equipment IS, as the Armoury and the smith name it. Distinct from the card domain: a Blade item type and a Blade card school are different facts about the same sword.

Where a starting card came from. The composed deck deals bound cards in this vocabulary's authored order, so adding a source is a row here rather than a code change. Nothing WEARS these — the `grant` family exists to declare them, the way `effect` declares which words a damage effect may carry.
Sprite selection only; never damage or resistance identity.
Source profile supplying an attack; separate from damage type.
How a direct attack reaches its targets.
Identity of a typed HP damage component.
Conditions for explicit technique bonuses.
Build synergies; tags alone grant no effects.

What a holder CONFERS while it is held. Each property node has exactly one entry in nodeEffects.json; the holder grants it, and it leaves when the holder does. EVERY family may carry one — what the mount path can hold (worn, owned, chosen) is the engine's narrower list, engine/properties.js MOUNTABLE_KINDS.
Steel and edge — direct weapon work.
Bracing, blocking, holding the line.
Bleed, and the letting of it.
The blood-and-flame stance.
Astral sorcery — charges and combos.
Rites, offerings, and faith work.
Creeping decay.
Binding, lasting commitments.
Finesse — footwork and multi-hit.
Spent once, then gone to ash.
Slow, committed, and hard to stop.
Everybody's — on the shelf without being found.
A precise physical form; presentation only.
Authored ranged presentation; no position system.
Deliberate aim and finesse; presentation only.
Preparation, misdirection, and stolen openings.
Poisons that punish enemies over time.
A smith can lift this card out of the item that lends it, and seat it in another item's mount. Strikes and defends do not carry it — today.
Carries its own cards — they arrive with the piece and are named in equipmentGrants.csv.
Animal, unreasoning, driven by hunger.
Two arms, two legs, and a reason for being here.
Died once and did not stay down.
Built, not born — no blood to let.
Untethered from the body it used to wear.
